subject: Finex - Throughput / SLO follow-up (latency, tokens/sec, peak vs steady)
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Finex discovery follow-up - throughput / SLO notes

Neha / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today — super helpful. As promised, here are the key pieces from our side to help with sizing and SLO recommendation: 

- Workload summary (high level):
  - Peak QPS: ~200 requests/sec (expected 2 short peak windows per day, ~6 hours total)
  - Steady QPS: ~25-35 requests/sec outside peak
  - Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens
  - Avg response tokens: 450 tokens
  - Typical request pattern: user types -> server issues 1 request; streaming preferred for long responses so the UI can show progressive output
  - Concurrency: ~80 average concurrent open sessions, spikes up to ~400 concurrent users in peak

- SLO targets we're aiming for: P95 time-to-first-token <= 350 ms, P95 end-to-end <= 1.2s for typical responses (<=2.5s for long tails). If streaming helps hit the first-token target we can relax end-to-end a bit.

I've attached a quick workbook (finex_workload_profile.xlsx) with an hour-by-hour sketch. Two asks: (1) can Redwood hit the P95 first-token under 350ms at peak QPS and concurrency? (2) rough tokens/sec numbers and whether we should plan for dedicated capacity vs hosted with burst?

Appreciate any initial guidance so we can prep procurement and our infra folks.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, Finex
alex.turner@finex.com
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex discovery follow-up - throughput / SLO notes

Alex / Priya — thanks for the detailed notes and the workbook. Quick post-call recap from our side and a couple clarifying Qs so we can size correctly: 

Recap:
- Peak is ~200 QPS for about 6 hours/day; steady 25-35 QPS otherwise.
- Average request ~570 tokens (prompt + response). Streaming required for UX.
- Concurrency during peak: spikes to ~400 concurrent users.
- Target: P95 first-token <= 350 ms.

Clarifying questions:
1) When you say "200 QPS peak", is that sustained across the entire 6-hour window or are there shorter micro-peaks inside that period?
2) For streaming: do you need token-by-token streaming or chunked streaming (e.g., first 128 tokens immediate, subsequent chunks every 100 tokens)?
3) Any hard constraints on model/quality vs cost tradeoffs (e.g., willing to accept a slightly smaller model to meet latency)?

Preliminary sizing notes (very rough):
- Tokens/sec at peak: 200 QPS * 570 tokens = 114,000 tokens/sec peak.
- Steady tokens/sec: 30 QPS * 570 = ~17,100 tokens/sec.
- We should model both peak token throughput and peak concurrency for memory/KV cache sizing. Streaming helps with perceived latency (first-token) but doesn't reduce total token compute.

Next steps: I want Rafael and Marissa to run a quick back-of-envelope estimate on GPU capacity and an initial perf profile (dedicated vs hosted). Rafael / Marissa — can you pick this up? Also we may need a short follow-up call with your infra lead to get sample traffic logs (anonymized) to do a tighter estimate.

I'll put together an initial options doc and pricing delta for dedicated capacity vs hosted with burst.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-23T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex discovery follow-up - throughput / SLO notes

Thanks Neha — quick answers inline: 
1) Peak shape: it's bursty within the 6-hour window. We see multiple 5-15 minute micro-peaks during business hours that approach the 200 QPS number; not perfectly sustained.
2) Streaming: chunked streaming is acceptable. Our UI streams first ~150 tokens quickly and then renders chunks (~150 tokens) every ~200ms. So first-token latency is the most important metric for UX.
3) Quality vs cost: we prefer to prioritize latency and reliability for the primary product flow; willing to evaluate a slightly smaller model for cost but only if output quality meets our internal evals.

I've uploaded the workbook and added a sheet with concurrency distribution and a sample 24-hour trace. Attaching finex_workload_profile.xlsx. Happy to get on a follow-up call with infra.

-Alex
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-24T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finex discovery follow-up - throughput / SLO notes

Appreciate the clarifications, Alex — that helps a lot. Quick plan and next steps: 

1) Rafael / Marissa will produce an initial throughput-sizing options doc by EOD 2027-03-26 that includes:
   - conservative dedicated-capacity estimate (GPU count and config) to meet P95 first-token <= 350ms at 200 QPS micro-peaks
   - hosted-with-burst profile (estimated token/sec headroom, recommended autoscale/burst settings)
   - cost ballpark for both options and recommended model/quantization tradeoffs

2) We'll also include a short note on streaming strategy (chunk sizes, prefix caching, and how it impacts first-token). Preliminary note: chunked streaming with prefix/KV caching should help hit first-token SLO while reducing tail compute.

3) Please share the anonymized 24-hour trace (we already saw the workbook) and confirm the Slack/Calendly link for an infra deep-dive — Rafael can join that session to go through memory/KV sizing details. If you prefer, we can do a short non-disclosure addendum before we ingest logs.

Rafael / Marissa — taking this to you. Alex / Priya — expect the options doc by EOD Friday (2027-03-26).

Thanks,
Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_throughput_summary.pdf (high-level reference), finex_workload_profile.xlsx (provided by customer)
